name: Switch
summary: An on/off setting that applies the moment it changes — focus-mode timer, theme follows system, reminders. Not for a choice collected by a form (Checkbox), not for an action (Button), never for consent. Two states only; no indeterminate, no invalid, no required.

children.requiredWhen: aria-label is not given. The visible label is the default; the type union refuses a switch with neither.
children.intent: The visible label AND the accessible name — the name of the setting, stated as what is on ('Focus timer', 'Follow system theme'), never as a question or an action. Rendered in a real <label>, so clicking the text toggles.

aria-label.requiredWhen: children is omitted (a switch at the end of a settings row whose text is already next to it).
aria-label.intent: Name without visible text. Must name the setting; 'Toggle' or 'On/off' says nothing.

onChange.intent: Fires with the new boolean (same shape as Checkbox). This is where the setting is applied — immediately, no Save button.

description.intent: Help text under the label, linked by aria-describedby — what the setting does, not what the switch is.

labelPlacement.intent: Where the text sits relative to the track. 'start' is the settings-list layout (text left, switch at the row's end); the DOM order and the name do not change.

isDisabled.intent: Removed from the tab order and from submission. Prefer isReadOnly when the state still matters to the user.

isReadOnly.intent: Focusable and announced, not toggleable — a setting locked by a plan or a policy the user must still be able to see.

value.intent: Native form value, for the rare switch inside a form.

size.intent: Row min-height 24 / 44 px (size.target.min / size.target.touch). The track is sized in em of the label's text so it scales with zoom; md is dense-settings density, lg is the touch default. No sm.

autoFocus.intent: Focus on mount. Rarely right for a setting.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to / from the switch. Each switch is its own tab stop.
Toggles on ↔ off and applies the setting at once.
Does nothing on the switch (native input behaviour, same as Checkbox). Inside a <form> it submits; the switch must not intercept it.

a11y.name: From children (a real <label> wrapping the input), or aria-label when children is omitted — the type union requires one of the two.
a11y.announcements: role="switch" with aria-checked true / false — read as 'on' / 'off' by screen readers, which is why the label must name the setting and not ask a question. description → aria-describedby. isReadOnly → aria-readonly="true"; still focusable and read.
a11y.targetSize: The whole label row is the target: md ≥ 24 px tall (2.5.8 AA minimum), lg ≥ 44 (touch). A bare switch without a label still gets a 24 px hit area around its track.

rules: A switch applies its setting the moment it changes (3.2.2: the change is the expected result of operating it, so no Save button and no confirmation). If the change needs a Save or a confirmation, it is a Checkbox in a form.
No validation props — no isInvalid, isRequired or errorMessage. A setting cannot be 'invalid' or 'required'; a required on/off is a Checkbox (consent) and it belongs in a form.
No indeterminate. A switch has two states; a mixed group of settings is a list of switches, not one mixed switch.

On is never colour-only: the thumb moves to the other end of the track (geometry) AND aria-checked is set. The track colour is the third cue, not the only one. In forced-colors mode the track keeps a FieldText border and the thumb uses the system colour, so on and off stay distinguishable in Windows High Contrast.
The label names the setting as a thing that can be on — 'Focus timer', not 'Do you want a timer?' and not 'Enable timer'. Screen readers append 'on' / 'off' to it.
Space toggles; Enter does not — do not add an Enter handler. Enter belongs to the form.
The label is a real <label> wrapping the input, so clicking anywhere on the text toggles. Never a <span> with an onClick.
Focus ring is outline + outline-offset on the track, never box-shadow alone.
Never for consent, never for a destructive setting without its own confirmation ('Delete account and data' is a Button with a confirm Modal, backlog 0e).

examples.title: Setting with description
examples.code: <Switch isSelected={timer} onChange={setTimer} description="25 minutes, then a short break.">Focus timer</Switch>

examples.title: Settings-list row (text first, switch at the end)
Locked by the plan
examples.code: <Switch isReadOnly isSelected description="Included in the 90-day pass.">Weekly summary email</Switch>

examples.title: Bare switch in a row that already shows the text
examples.code: <Switch aria-label="Reminders for overdue actions" isSelected={reminders} onChange={setReminders} />
